items.title: Finding the Side Length of a Cube Given the Length of Its Face Diagonal

sections.normalized_html: Given that [MATH: BE = 15\sqrt{2} \, \text{cm},] find the side length of the cube.
sections.readable_text:
Given that [MATH: BE = 15\sqrt{2} \, \text{cm},] find the side length of the cube.

[IMG: /graphics/17ba4f3b4e2d6277ab90dd1ec4766e58]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Notice that [MATH: \overline{BE}] is a face diagonal of the cube.

Since the length of a face diagonal [MATH: f] of a cube can be found using the formula

[MATH: f = s \sqrt{2},]

where [MATH: s] is the length of an edge, we can find [MATH: s] as follows:

[MATH: s = \dfrac{f}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{15\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 15]

Therefore, the length of the edges is [MATH: 15 \, \text{cm}.]

[IMG: /graphics/17ba4f3b4e2d6277ab90dd1ec4766e58]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Notice that [MATH: \overline{BE}] is a face diagonal of the cube.

Since the length of a face diagonal [MATH: f] of a cube can be found using the formula

[MATH: f = s \sqrt{2},]

where [MATH: s] is the length of an edge, we can find [MATH: s] as follows:

[MATH: s = \dfrac{f}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{15\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 15]

Therefore, the length of the edges is [MATH: 15 \, \text{cm}.]

Item 9 — Tutorial: Deriving the Face Diagonal Length Formula

Content:
Here, we will derive the formula [MATH: f=s\sqrt{2}] that we have been using throughout this lesson.

Content:
Consider a cube of side length [MATH: s] and face diagonal length [MATH: f,] like the one shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/2079f5ec5123e736cd1e1d1fd2cb0e28]

Content:
Notice that [MATH: \triangle ABC] is a right triangle with legs [MATH: AB] and [MATH: AC] and hypotenuse [MATH: BC.] Therefore, by the Pythagorean theorem, we have

Content:
[MATH: s^{2} + s^{2}|= f^{2}; 2s^{2}|= f^{2}; f|= sqrt(2s^{2}); f|= sqrt(2) ⋅ sqrt(s^{2}); f|= sqrt(2) ⋅ s; f|= ssqrt(2).]

Content:
Notice that we only consider the positive square root since [MATH: f] is a length and therefore must be positive.
